newsitem.title: CHINA: China says Tibet monks hail Panchen anniversary.
newsitem.headline: China says Tibet monks hail Panchen anniversary.

text.p: Monks in Tibet have celebrated the first anniversary of Beijing's selection of the Himalayan region's second holiest monk, official media said on Monday.

Officials said last week that seven-year-old Gyaincain Norbu, pushed by Beijing as the 11th incarnation of the Panchen Lama, spent the anniversary quietly in Beijing, far from the region where he is widely rejected.
Tibet's spiritual leader, the exiled Dalai Lama, has named another boy as the reincarnation of the 10th Panchen Lama, the Himalayan region's second holiest monk who died in 1989.

The Xinhua news agency and major newspapers said monks at Tashilunpo Lamasery, the seat of the Panchen Lama, celebrated the Friday anniversary of his appointment and the placing in the monastery of an inscription by President Jiang Zemin promoting patriotism.
It gave no details of the celebrations.

Western watchdog groups have reported that members of the Tibetan Buddhist clergy, long an area of separatist sentiment, have come under increasing pressure from propaganda officials to pledge allegiance to the Beijing-anointed Panchen Lama.
Chinese sources have said Beijing's choice currently lives in the capital under state protection against any possible assassination attempts by radical Tibetans.
